description: FIRST CLEARING-PLANE MIRROR GOLDEN (code review 2026-07-25, regression B — the cut-aware mirror SILENTLY NO-OPPED the 'complete the symmetric half' workflow, the #1 mirror idiom after 'hole on both sides'. `_prev_cut_tools` fires whenever the immediately-preceding body-affecting feature is an extrude-cut or a Hole, and the mirror then took `mirror_cut` UNCONDITIONALLY; `mirror_cut` never verified anything was removed, so a reflected tool that lands OUTSIDE the body cut nothing, the lump count was unchanged, and the untouched body came back with every feature 'ok'. The user's part was never completed and no error was raised). A 40 x 40 mm square sketched on the XY datum and extruded 20 mm into the block [0,40] x [0,40] x [0,20]; a second XY sketch [10,20] x [10,30] extruded 10 mm as a CUT, notching the block's -Z face; a YZ-parallel offset datum at x=40 — the block's own +X FACE, a CLEARING plane the body only touches; then a MIRROR about that datum. Because the reflected pocket tool (x in [60,70]) cannot reach the body, the mirror reads as 'reflect and union the BODY' — and the reflection of an already-pocketed body carries its own pocket — so the result is the completed 80 mm part with a notch in EACH half, fused across the shared x=40 face into ONE solid. The pre-fix behaviour returned the unchanged 30000 mm^3 block at x in [0,40], so volume, surface area, centroid, AABB, topology AND mesh counts all discriminate the fix. The OVERLAPPING (own-midplane) reading is unchanged and regression-guarded by mirror-hole-feature-plate-40x40x20; the plain reflect-and-union path by mirror-triangle-prism-2x. Deliberately ALL-PLANAR (no bore) so every expectation below is exactly hand-derivable; the hole -> clearing-plane-mirror chain, which shares this code path with Hole-sourced tools, is covered by test_mirror.py rather than a second curved golden.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, then confirmed against the harness (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Every face is planar, so the derivation is exact arithmetic.

block: outer square x,y in [0,40] on XY (4 lines, no constraints -> zero residual, planegcs returns input positions bitwise), extruded 20 mm along +Z = [0,40] x [0,40] x [0,20], volume 40*40*20 = 32000 mm^3.

pocket: the second sketch x in [10,20], y in [10,30] extruded 10 mm as a CUT along +Z removes [10,20] x [10,30] x [0,10] = 10*20*10 = 2000 mm^3, a blind rectangular notch open ONLY on the -Z face. Source body = 32000 - 2000 = 30000 mm^3.
mirror plane: a datum parallel to the YZ origin plane (normal +X) slid +40 mm -> the plane x=40, which IS the block's +X face. The body TOUCHES it and clears it (no volume beyond x=40).

mirror: the reflected pocket tool lands at x in [60,70] — outside the body — so the reflected removal cannot reach it and the mirror reflects+unions the BODY (vacuous-cut fallback). The reflection is [40,80] x [0,40] x [0,20] minus its own notch at x in [60,70], y in [10,30], z in [0,10]. Source and reflection share the whole x=40 face, so the fuse+clean gives ONE solid spanning [0,80] with two notches, mirror-symmetric about x=40.
volume = 2 * 30000 = 60000 mm^3 (the two halves are disjoint apart from the zero-volume shared face). The pre-fix silent no-op gives 30000 — this value FAILS on the old behaviour by 2x.

surface_area: outer box [0,80] x [0,40] x [0,20] = 2*(80*40) + 2*(80*20) + 2*(40*20) = 6400 + 3200 + 1600 = 11200; minus the two notch mouths on the -Z face (2 * 10*20 = 400); plus each notch's interior (two 20x10 walls = 400, two 10x10 walls = 200, one 10x20 roof = 200 -> 800 each, 1600 for both) = 11200 - 400 + 1600 = 12400 mm^2. The shared x=40 face is INTERIOR after the fuse and contributes nothing (a failed clean would show up here).

centroid = (40, 20, 31/3): x and y by symmetry (the part is mirror-symmetric about x=40, and both notches are centred on y=20); z = (2*32000*10 - 2*2000*5) / 60000 = (640000 - 20000) / 60000 = 620000/60000 = 10.333333333333334 mm — the notches sit in the lower half, so the centroid rides ABOVE mid-height. A no-op result would also give z = 31/3 (same shape), so z does NOT discriminate; the VOLUME, AABB and face count do.
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[80,40,20]: the mirror doubles the x extent, the sole AABB change.

topology: 16 faces = 6 outer box faces (the -Z face carries both notch mouths as INNER loops, still one face) + 5 per notch (4 walls + 1 roof) * 2; 36 edges = 12 outer box edges + 12 per notch (4 mouth + 4 vertical + 4 roof) * 2; 1 shell (the halves fuse across x=40 — a failed fuse would read 2).

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular default): all faces planar, so deflection is non-binding and every face triangulates from its corners alone. -Z face: 4 outer + 2*4 hole-loop nodes = 12 vertices, 12 - 2 + 2*2 = 14 triangles (the with-holes planar count used by the 2-hole plate goldens). +Z face: 4 / 2. Four outer side walls: 4*(4 / 2) = 16 / 8. Ten notch faces: 10*(4 / 2) = 40 / 20. Totals 12+4+16+40 = 72 vertices, 14+2+8+20 = 44 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing).
GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned: it is asserted byte-deterministic by the runner within a kernel version, but the absolute size has no geometric meaning across glTF-writer upgrades.
tolerance_rationale: PLANAR boolean tolerance, measured first then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). Every face is planar and the mirror is an exact isometry, so the only residual is GProp accumulation through the cut + fuse. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-25, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs): volume |60000 - 59999.99999999999| ~ 1.5e-11, surface_area ~ 1.8e-12, centroid.z ~ 1.8e-15, centroid.x/.y and all AABB bounds exactly 0.0. The documented 1e-9 ceiling — the established planar-golden bound shared with boolean-subtract-two-cubes-overlap and mirror-triangle-prism-2x, and 100x TIGHTER than the standing 1e-7 kernel linear bound — covers the worst measured residual with ~65x headroom for libm/BLAS/platform variation across CI hosts. Topology and mesh counts carry NO tolerance (exact-match). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
